metaDescription: Discover the 4 essential monthly financial reports every Nepalese business owner must review. Catch debtor issues, manage VAT ledgers, and protect margins.
h1: Which Financial Reports Should a Small Business Review Monthly?
directAnswer: A small business in Nepal should review four primary financial reports monthly: the Profit and Loss (P&L) Statement to evaluate operational profitability, the Balance Sheet to monitor solvency and debt, the Aged Accounts Receivable Report to track overdue customer credit, and the Bank Reconciliation Statement to verify that accounting software records match bank balances exactly.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.h2: The 4 Essential Monthly Financial Reports Every Business Needs
sections.contentHtml:
Running a commercial business in Nepal without monthly management reports is like driving through fog without headlights. Executive decision-makers cannot wait for the annual audit in Poush to understand whether operations were profitable in Shrawan. A structured monthly financial review package consists of four core statements:

1. Monthly Profit & Loss (Income Statement)

Displays gross revenue, cost of sales (COGS), operating overheads, and net profit before tax for the preceding 30 days compared against budgeted targets.

2. Statement of Financial Position (Balance Sheet)

Provides an instantaneous snapshot of current assets (bank cash, inventory, debtor receivables) versus current liabilities (supplier payables, tax obligations, bank overdrafts).

3. Rolling 13-Week Cash-Flow Projection

Maps incoming cash collections against guaranteed monthly outflows (salaries, SSF, office rent, bank EMI) to prevent mid-month payroll defaults.

4. Aged Debtor & Creditor Ledger (A/R & A/P)

Classifies outstanding customer balances into 0-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, and 90+ days past due to trigger immediate collections.

sections.h2: Core Financial Ratios to Review in Your Monthly Meeting
sections.contentHtml:
Beyond raw numbers, managers should review three vital operational health indicators every month:

  • Gross Margin Percentage: (Gross Profit / Revenue) * 100. If this drops below historical norms, supplier pricing has increased without matching retail price adjustments.
  • Current Ratio: Current Assets / Current Liabilities. Should ideally remain above 1.30 to ensure sufficient liquidity to service short-term debts.
  • Days Sales Outstanding (DSO): The average number of days required to collect payment after issuing a tax invoice. In Nepal, a DSO exceeding 65 days signals acute credit collection bottlenecks.

sections.h2: Establishing a Reconciled Monthly Reporting Calendar
sections.contentHtml: A disciplined monthly cadence requires closing ledgers by the 7th of every Nepali month, executing bank reconciliations by the 10th, and holding a structured executive review by the 15th. Learn how our accounting and bookkeeping services in Nepal institutionalize this discipline for growing companies.

faqs.question: Who should participate in the monthly financial review meeting?
faqs.answer: At minimum, the managing director, operations head, and primary financial advisor or senior accountant should participate to review variances against budget and approve credit limits.

faqs.question: Can accounting software automate these four monthly reports?
faqs.answer: Yes. Modern cloud and desktop accounting solutions generate these reports instantly, provided all daily vouchers, bank entries, and inventory receipts are reconciled and closed timely.
